instruction: Change the editor font size to 18 in VS Code settings.

metadata.trajectory_summary: Agent opened VS Code settings, navigated File > Open Workspace from File, successfully opened workspace1.code-workspace, attempted to add workspace2 folders, then correctly identified opening two workspaces in the same window as infeasible.
metadata.capability_extraction: Can navigate VS Code menus, open workspace files via File dialog, use keyboard shortcuts (Ctrl+`, F1, Ctrl+Shift+P), interact with file manager, access VS Code settings page
metadata.task_rationale: Model demonstrated ability to navigate VS Code settings (first screenshot shows Settings page with search). This task tests modifying a specific setting value.
metadata.explanation: Task requires changing editor.fontSize to 18 in VS Code settings. Evaluator uses official check_json_settings metric to verify settings.json contains the expected value.

llm_judge_reasons: Getter vscode_config correctly extracts settings.json from the right path (/home/user/.config/Code/User/settings.json) by opening the VS Code command palette and running 'Preferences: Open Settings (JSON)'
Metric check_json_settings correctly parses the JSON file and checks that editor.fontSize equals 18, which is exactly what the instruction requires
Expected value structure is correct: get_rule returns {'expected': {'editor.fontSize': 18}}, and check_json_settings accesses expected['expected'] to get the key-value pairs to verify
Complete coverage: the instruction has a single requirement (change editor font size to 18) and the evaluator verifies exactly that
The static warning about str type hint on check_json_settings second parameter is cosmetic — Python does not enforce type hints at runtime, and the code correctly handles the dict

rule_validation_issues.msg: metric check_json_settings second parameter type (str) may not match expected.rules type (Dict)
